title: Ingest Sentinel: progressive schema arbitration and QoS shaper
creator: Lena Cho
description: Build a lightweight, extensible ingest coordinator (Ingest Sentinel) that performs progressive schema arbitration for usage events and applies adaptive QoS shaping. The goal is to reduce downstream schema errors, avoid full ingestion pipeline failures, and maintain latency SLOs by classifying events into strict/lenient/transform flows and applying circuit breakers and backpressure at the edge.
acceptance_criteria: New ingest sentinel service deployed behind feature flag for 10% of traffic
Events validated with three-tier arbitration (strict, lenient, transform) with >=95% of previously failing events routed to lenient or transform paths in canary
End-to-end median ingest latency increase <= 5ms at p50 and p95 during canary
Clear telemetry: per-route invalidation rates, transform success rate, dropped-event counts, and upstream error attribution available in Console dashboards
Fallback circuit triggers and automated rollback exercised in chaos test with documented runbook
technical_notes: Architecture: a stateless fronting service (Sentinel) receives usage events, applies fast shape checks (compiled validation rules), consults a lightweight policy cache, and assigns each event to one of three paths: STRICT (reject+NACK), LENIENT (accept+annotate), TRANSFORM (apply deterministic fixups then accept).

Validation engine: use a compiled rule set (Horn-like match patterns) that runs in <1ms on typical event payloads. Rules authored as canonical JSON Schema snippets plus small hook scripts for common fixups (timestamp normalization, legacy field mapping).
Policy cache: single-node LRU with SSE-based refresh for rapid rollout of schema changes. Policies are versioned and pinned per customer to support gradual model rollouts.

QoS shaping: implement circuit breakers based on error rate and backpressure via leaky-bucket per-tenant queues. If queue depth exceeds threshold, automatically route new events to a best-effort async store (S3 archive) and emit alert.

Observability: emit fine-grained events for validation decisions (decision_type, rule_id, duration_ms) and histogram of route latencies. Tag metrics with customer_id, route, and model_tag to enable cost attribution in Console.
Security: do not persist PII during lenient path; transformations must redact sensitive fields according to KMS policy. All policy changes require an audit log entry.
Backward-compatibility: sentinel supports per-workload compatibility levels. Default for existing customers is lenient to avoid disruption; opt-in strict for new customers after pre-validation.

Compatibility with existing systems: sentinel will call existing ingestion Kafka topic 'usage-events-validated' for strict/lenient and 'usage-events-transform' for transformed events. A small adapter will translate older envelope formats into the canonical envelope expected by the sentinel.
implementation_plan: Week 1: prototype validation engine with compiled JSON Schema runner + sample rule set; basic decision telemetry
Week 2: implement policy cache and per-tenant policy pins; add atomic policy rollout API
Week 3: add QoS shaping primitives (per-tenant leaky bucket) and async archive sink for overflow
Week 4: integrate transform hooks and implement deterministic fixups for top 5 observed schema failures
Week 5: end-to-end tests, load tests (0.5x to 3x current peak), and security review
Week 6: deploy behind feature flag to 10% traffic; monitor metrics and iterate
Week 7: increase rollout to 50% then 100% with staggered tenant cohorts; complete runbook and handoff
rollout_strategy: Feature flagged rollout: start 10% synthetic + low-risk tenants
Canary goals: validation failure rate reduction, no SLO regression, transform accuracy > 90% for fixed rules
SLOs to monitor: ingest end-to-end p95 latency, downstream consumer lag, and dropped-event rate
Rollback: immediate feature-flag revert if dropped-event rate increases > 0.1% absolute or if p95 latency regression > 20%
Post-deploy: 48h intensive monitoring window with on-call eng and PM assigned
risks_mitigation: Risk: Mis-classification of events leading to silent data loss. Mitigation: conservative default routing to lenient path with archival of raw events for 30 days until policy stabilized.
Risk: Added latency at front door. Mitigation: micro-benchmark validation implementation, fast-path cache for well-known customers, and feature flag to disable transforms if latency breaches target.
Risk: Transform rules introducing data corruption. Mitigation: deterministic transforms, property-based tests and a transformation sandbox; require approval workflow for new transform rules.
Risk: Operational complexity for policy management. Mitigation: build a simple web UI for policy inspection and rollback hooks; require policy change audit logs and automated tests on policy changes.
comments: 2026-01-12 Lena Cho: Initial ticket created after post-mortem showed 12% of ingest failures were schema-related transient errors. Proposal: reduce blast radius by routing to lenient/transform paths and archive raw events for debugging.

2026-01-20 Marco Alvarez: Prototype validation engine benchmarks: compiled-rule approach runs at ~700ns/op on dev box for small events. Suggest using bulk rule evaluation and fast-path cache for top 80% shapes.
2026-01-28 Priya Nair (PM): Reviewed acceptance criteria. Asked to add explicit metric for transform success rate and to ensure 30-day archival retention is documented.

2026-02-03 Security review (Jake Morales): Called out requirement to redact PII in lenient path and to ensure transforms are not reversible to raw PII. Added security_review_required flag to rollout checklist.
2026-02-10 QA (Yara Ibrahim): End-to-end tests added for three canonical failure modes. Found one flakey transform for legacy timestamp format; fixed normalization rule and re-ran tests.

2026-02-15 Marco Alvarez: Deployed canary to 10% traffic (low-risk tenants). Early telemetry: invalidation rate down 78% for canary cohort; transform success 93%; p95 latency unchanged. Continuing monitoring.
